sources.entry: Programming Language Checklist: a fun take on "so you want to build your own language?"

summary.title: Programming Language Checklist
summary.one_liner: A satirical checkbox list of the common objections experienced programming-language designers hear about their new language, from syntax debates to missing tooling and unsupported benchmarks.
keywords: so you want to build your own language
takeaways: Language designers often underestimate needs like concurrency, REPL, debugger and IDE support, and I/O.
Common criticisms include unsupported productivity or ease-of-use claims and rigged benchmarks that just call handwritten assembly, PCRE, or BLAS.
Tooling, a clear language spec, and ecosystem fit matter as much as syntax.
The list is humorous: it is a set of checkboxes to tick when someone proposes a new language.
summary.summary: This page is a satirical checklist, written by Colin McMillen, Jason Reed, and Elly Fong-Jones in 2011, that mocks the typical critiques a new programming language receives. It uses checkbox-style lists covering paradigms, beliefs about syntax and memory, missing features, philosophical objections, implementation flaws, marketing claims, and ecosystem comparisons. It contains no code or tutorial steps; the value is in the list of common pitfalls and objections in language design.
